T: Crème de la crème. Hold the sleeping pills.
D: A family of pampered Paris cats is dumped in the countryside by the butler and finds its way home with an alley cat.
P: Serve dessert when Edgar the butler prepares the cream.
S: Blue cheese with sliced pears, walnuts, honey and water crackers
Wedges of blue cheese on a board with sliced pears, toasted walnuts, a pot of honey and crackers.

Choux pastry with gruyère piped into small balls, baked at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed. Bring 125ml water, 125ml milk, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until the dough comes away from the sides. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy. Stir in 120g grated gruyère, a pinch of nutmeg and pepper. Pipe walnut-size balls onto lined trays, top with a little more cheese and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
Ham and gruyere sandwiches topped with bechamel and more cheese
Mini croque monsieurs of ham, gruyère, Dijon and béchamel on white bread, grilled until bubbling and cut into squares.
M: Chicken thighs braised in red grape juice with bacon and mushrooms
Chicken thighs browned and simmered with bacon, mushrooms and red grape juice for 90 minutes, with buttery mash.
Abigail and Amelia's chicken leek pie
Abigail and Amelia, the English geese

Chicken, leek and mushroom pie in a creamy sauce under puff pastry, baked at 200C for 25 minutes. Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in 30g butter and set aside. Cook 1 sliced leek and 200g sliced mushrooms for 6 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick. Add the chicken and thyme and season. Spoon into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve with buttered peas.
W: Baked vanilla bean custard in ramekins
Vanilla crème brûlée baked at 150C for 35 minutes in a water bath, chilled, sugar torched on top. Nothing added.
K: Vanilla bean, ice cream, milk and honey blended

Cold milk blended with vanilla ice cream, honey and a vanilla bean until frothy, poured into glasses with a pinch of nutmeg on top. Split 1 vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into a blender, or use 1 tsp vanilla bean paste. Add 600ml cold full cream milk, 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 2 tbsp honey and blend for 30 seconds until frothy. Pour into 4 glasses and dust with a little grated nutmeg. Serve straight away.

note.text: Manners, kittens. Even when the world turns upside down.

winks: Thomas O'Malley and his alley cats

dishes.make_ahead: Toast the walnuts up to 3 days ahead, airtight; slice the pears and set out the cheese on the night

steps.text: Set the cheese out at room temperature.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan.
Slice the pears thinly and fan them beside the cheese.
Add the walnuts, honey and crackers.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the bechamel up to 2 days ahead with cling film on the surface, chilled; assemble and grill on the night

steps.text: Make a bechamel from the butter, flour and milk.
Spread the bread with Dijon, fill with ham and gruyere and arrange on a tray.
Top with bechamel and more grated cheese.
Grill until bubbling.
Cut into small squares and serve on a silver tray.

veg.make_ahead: Fry the mushrooms and make the bechamel up to 1 day ahead, kept chilled; assemble and grill on the night

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in a third of the butter until golden.
Make a bechamel from the rest of the butter, the flour and milk.
Spread the bread with Dijon, fill with mushrooms and grated cheese and arrange on a tray.
Top with bechamel and more grated cheese.
Grill until bubbling.
Cut into small squares and serve on a silver tray.

dishes.make_ahead: The braise keeps up to 2 days chilled, reheat gently; mash the potatoes on the night

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and slice the mushrooms.
Brown the chicken and bacon.
Add the mushrooms and cook until golden.
Pour in the red grape juice and water to cover and simmer.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter.

veg.make_ahead: Simmer the mushrooms and beans in the grape juice up to 2 days ahead and reheat gently; mash the potatoes on the night

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and halve the mushrooms.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil in batches with the smoked paprika.
Pour in the red grape juice and stock, add the butter beans and simmer until glossy.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter.
Split the vanilla bean and heat with the cream until steaming.
Heat.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar for the custard and pour in the cream. Strain into ramekins.
Bake in a water bath at 150C.
Chill.
Sprinkle with the sugar for the top and torch until amber.

dishes.make_ahead: Best blended just before serving so it stays thick and frothy; the vanilla bean can steep in the milk up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Split the bean and scrape the seeds into a blender.
Add the milk, ice cream and honey and blend until frothy.
Pour into four glasses and dust with nutmeg.

s.note: Blue cheese with sliced pears, walnuts, honey and water crackers
s.how: Set a wedge of blue cheese at room temperature on a wooden board. Slice 2 pears thinly and fan them beside it. Add toasted walnuts, a pot of honey and water crackers. A board fit for a mouse with very good taste.

s.note: Ham and gruyere sandwiches topped with bechamel and more cheese
s.how: Make a quick bechamel with 30g butter, a spoon of flour and 250ml milk. Spread bread with Dijon, fill with ham and grated gruyere, then top with bechamel and more cheese. Grill until bubbling and cut into small squares. Serve on a silver tray.

m.note: Chicken thighs braised in red grape juice and stock with bacon and mushrooms
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs and 150g diced bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in 500ml red grape juice and water to cover. Simmer for 90 minutes until rich and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and butter.

w.note: Baked vanilla bean custard in ramekins
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch until amber. Nothing added.

d.note: Vanilla bean, ice cream, milk and honey blended
d.how: Split 1 vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into a blender, or use 1 tsp vanilla bean paste. Add 600ml cold full cream milk, 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 2 tbsp honey and blend for 30 seconds until frothy. Pour into 4 glasses and dust with a little grated nutmeg. Serve straight away.
